title: Existing-Home Sales (NAR, August 2026 data) — the corridor's widest session for homebuilders, and none of the width is this print, 10:00 a.m. ET
source: IR: the publisher's own forward calendar — nar.realtor/press-releases/nar-statistical-news-release-schedule (fetched direct 2026-09-08, HTTP 200, 483,177 bytes), whose 2026 table reads verbatim "SEPTEMBER | Thu., Sep. 10 | August Existing-Home Sales" under the page's standing note "All releases at 10 a.m. Eastern Time"; its downloadable twin /sites/default/files/2025-11/2026-nar-statistical-news-release-schedule.docx (HTTP 200, 55,384 bytes, published 2025-11), unzipped and read as XML, carries the identical September row; and NAR's live statistics page nar.realtor/research-and-statistics/housing-statistics/existing-home-sales (HTTP 200, 588,410 bytes) states verbatim "Existing-Home Sales for August 2026 will be released on Thursday, September 10, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern". Promoted from the `EST:` proposal filed 2026-09-08 by the fomc-2026-09-16 sweep, on exactly the precedent existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 used on the identical page (challenger-job-cuts-2026-09-03: a private publisher's own release carries IR:/confirmed; NAR is the producer of this series, not an aggregator). Corroborated a fourth way: the Atlanta Fed's own GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet (fetched direct 2026-09-08) schedules a 2026-09-10 10:00 posting naming "Wholesale trade, Producer Price Index, Existing-home sales". Checked 2026-09-08
notes: The August edition, and the inverse of its own sibling. existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 is this calendar's CLEAN edition — unscheduled by the Atlanta Fed, expected to post a SOLO vintage, in a month with no FOMC. 09-10 is the CROWDED one: the Fed's forward schedule names it with THREE releases (Wholesale trade, PPI, Existing-home sales), it sits inside the 2026-09-05 -> 2026-09-17 FOMC communications blackout with no Fed voice available, it shares 08:30 with PPI, 13:00 with a 30-year bond auction and the morning with the ECB, and the August CPI lands the next morning. Two regimes own that session and NEITHER is this print, both measured this session on 2,514 daily sessions 2016-09-06 -> 2026-09-04 (Nasdaq API; VIX from CBOE): the FOMC BLACKOUT widens homebuilders and only homebuilders — across 678 blackout sessions ITB's median range is 2.003% against 1.838% (permutation p<0.001) and XHB 1.784% against 1.610% (p<0.001) while SPY is untouched at 0.882% vs 0.885% (p=0.948) — and SAME-SESSION PPI widens the index and only the index, 108 PPI vintage days giving SPY 1.030% against 0.879% (p=0.038) with ITB p=0.650 and XHB p=0.961. The print itself stays inert on every cut: 114 EHS release days leave ITB (p=0.57), XHB (p=0.46) and SPY (p=0.65) at baseline; the 36 that fell inside a blackout are no wider than the 78 outside (ITB 1.859% vs 1.927%, p=0.53); and the session one trading day BEFORE a CPI vintage — this print's other shape — is flat at n=107 (ITB 1.862% vs 1.873%, p=0.89). So impact stays `low` and no instrument attaches. On the nowcast side the shared vintage is a warning, not a bonus: solo EHS vintages move the change-in-inventory-investment contribution a median 0.0001pp and clear 0.0010pp only 17 times in 123, while all 6 of the >=3-release shared ones clear it, so 09-10's inventories and headline lines will move for WHOLESALE-TRADE reasons; residential is the only EHS-attributable leaf and stays equally clean either way (|delta|<0.10pp on 83.3% of shared vs 81.3% of solo). One correction handed back to two siblings: the existing-home-sales-2026-12-09 kill switch names 09-10 as a dated chance to observe ITB >3.0%, and the VIX<=16 clause existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 added to it is still not enough — blackout sessions at VIX<=16 clear 3.0% at 7.5% (22/293) against 5.0% (53/1051) for all low-VIX sessions, so as amended the switch would fire on 09-10 for regime reasons and read as a housing signal. Date is `confirmed` on the publisher's own calendar; that licenses nothing, and the ledger's call is stand aside on every horizon. Discovered in the fomc-2026-09-16 adjacency sweep 2026-09-08; canonical file written by this event's own initial research the same day, which shadows that proposal.
